prompt: List the workspaces that contain a channel with a message which received a 🚀 (rocket) reaction from an admin of that same workspace.
binding_note: The reactor's single workspace-membership role must be admin in the SAME workspace that owns the channel/message reacted on. Every reactor in this scenario is deliberately given exactly one workspace membership (per the runtime rule that users.info exposes one selected workspace association), so the admin-role check for a reactor is a single, well-defined lookup compared against the team_id of the reacted-on channel — no per-team role disambiguation is required.

obligations.name: qualifying_workspaces
obligations.description: Workspaces that contain a channel holding a message which received a rocket-emoji reaction from a user whose sole workspace-membership role is admin in that same workspace.
obligations.scope: workspaces reachable via channel->message->reaction->user->workspace-membership chain matching the admin/rocket condition

task_spec.text: Identify and list every workspace that has a channel with a message reacted to by a rocket emoji from an admin of that same workspace.

access_plan: Enumerate workspaces via teams. For each workspace, use conversations.list (team_id scoped) to enumerate its channels and conversations.history to pull their messages, then reactions.get per message to see each reactor and emoji name. For every rocket reactor, call users.info once to read their single exposed workspace association (team_id + role); a reactor qualifies a workspace only if that one returned team_id equals the channel's team_id and the returned role is admin. Because every reactor in this scenario is seeded with exactly one workspace membership, this single lookup per reactor is sufficient and unambiguous. Aggregate the team_ids that satisfy this into the final list.
